The register says applicant: "Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik GmbH"
The document says applicant: "Flintec GmbH"

These are two genuinely different company names. Hottinger Baldwin Messtechnik (HBM) is a German measurement technology company. Flintec is also a German (originally Swedish) weighing technology company. These are clearly different entities — not spelling drift, not legal-suffix drift, not OCR noise.

Per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

So verdict: different-entity, best_value: "Flintec GmbH".

The actual certificate text is the legal instrument.

Possibly the register is wrong or referencing a different certificate. Either way, the rules are clear: genuinely different company names → different-entity, best_value from document.
